parts.visual:
You and your co-founder have been fighting for six months. The stress is destroying the company. One of you has to leave. It is financially and emotionally brutal.

The Reality:
1. Co-founder conflict is the #1 reason early-stage startups die.
2. The Divorce: Firing your co-founder is exactly like a marriage divorce. It involves lawyers, massive emotional trauma, and the complex un-tangling of the Cap Table (Equity).
parts.audio: Firing a co-founder is the most traumatic event in a startup's lifecycle. It is highly emotional, legally dangerous, and if handled incorrectly, it will instantly destroy the company.

questions.question: You decide to fire your co-founder. They have a 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff. They are fired on month 14. What happens to their equity?
options: They only keep the exact amount that vested during those 14 months (roughly 29%). The remaining 71% of their unvested stock is legally taken back by the company. They are now an ex-employee, but still a minority shareholder.
questions.correct_answer: They only keep the exact amount that vested during those 14 months (roughly 29%). The remaining 71% of their unvested stock is legally taken back by the company. They are now an ex-employee, but still a minority shareholder.
questions.explanation: This is exactly why the vesting schedule exists. Without it, the fired co-founder would walk away with half your company.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO talking to the Board of Directors. Why must they act so quickly to fire the co-founder?
questions.tts_text: He is toxic. The engineers are threatening to quit because of his behavior. If we don't remove him from the building by Friday, the entire engineering team will walk out.
options: Culture Protection. A toxic co-founder will act like a cancer, driving away all the 'A-Players' in the company. The Board must surgically remove the founder to save the rest of the team.
questions.correct_answer: Culture Protection. A toxic co-founder will act like a cancer, driving away all the 'A-Players' in the company. The Board must surgically remove the founder to save the rest of the team.
questions.explanation: Tolerance of a toxic co-founder signals to the rest of the company that toxicity is acceptable.

questions.question: What is the biggest mistake founders make when starting a company that guarantees a terrible 'Divorce' later?
options: Not signing an Operating Agreement on Day 1. If you don't write down the legal rules of 'how we fire each other' when you are best friends, it will be a legal bloodbath when you become enemies.
questions.correct_answer: Not signing an Operating Agreement on Day 1. If you don't write down the legal rules of 'how we fire each other' when you are best friends, it will be a legal bloodbath when you become enemies.
questions.explanation: You must plan the divorce before you get married.

questions.question: Can the CEO just fire the other Co-Founder by yelling 'You're fired'?
options: Yes, if they are loud enough.

Usually no. Co-founders are typically members of the Board of Directors. To remove a founder, you usually need a formal vote from the Board, and it must be executed strictly according to the corporate bylaws.
questions.correct_answer: Usually no. Co-founders are typically members of the Board of Directors. To remove a founder, you usually need a formal vote from the Board, and it must be executed strictly according to the corporate bylaws.
questions.explanation: Firing a founder is a complex corporate governance action, not a simple HR decision.

questions.explanation: Vesting schedules and Operating Agreements are your insurance policy against human emotion.
